## Purpose

Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (fleet-runtime).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: supporting - G3 depends on it, and today's alternative is ideas typed into 1 orchestrator conversation; rule 3 (diff 6 with cplx 5 is below the core rule); cplx 5 because fleetd code runs 1 fixed idea state machine and the judgment work is done by the sub-orchestrator model (A1, decision D1 open). Medium investment: it feeds the core task-execution with committed plans. — _future_: Hidden core: the hard part (research, interview, assumptions, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model. Keep the dispatcher flat; give plan validation and the approval hash invariant tests. Re-check the type at review (D1, Q1).

## Domain roles

**specification-model**, **approver** — It builds a document, the plan, that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3) and then executed by task-execution: a specification model. It holds the operator approval gate, where an idea goes on only with the operator's approved hash (FR-10, I7): an approver. Decision D2 is open ([define A18]).

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Idea** | A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it | ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea), request |
| **Sub-Orchestrator** | The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase | orchestrator, lead |
| **Assumption** | 1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11) | requirement |
| **Plan** | The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan | ticket list |
| **Spec** | spec.md and requirements.yaml of 1 idea. Every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. It is written only after approval, in the phase specifying (FR-10). | — |
| **Question** | A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator | — |
| **Orchestrator** | Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3) | — |

## Business decisions

1. Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).
2. An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).
3. The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.
4. While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.
5. When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).
6. A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).
7. Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).
8. A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded; past its time limit the question escalates to needs-you/ (RR-12, discover Q2 for the limit).
9. The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13).
10. When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.
11. When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).
12. Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles launch-environment and fleet-runtime start-agent-process (connect N3).

## Assumptions

- [understand A3] horch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage. (confidence medium)
- [understand A7] The alternatives are inferred from the design and the research files: today's horch with 1 orchestrator conversation, agents run by hand, and hosted merge queues (GitHub merge queue, bors, Mergify). (confidence medium)
- [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)
- [discover A2] The 5 phases and 4 pivotal events are a hypothesis drawn from the idea state machine (captured to merged) and the landing state machine. Decision D1 records the alternatives. (confidence medium)
- [discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high)
- [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)
- [discover A8] Feature Opened happens after Assumptions Written for an idea with no --to, as the Features section says; the idea row records its feature at capture only for --to (H7). (confidence low)
- [discover A10] Event count 82 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)
- [decompose A3] The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Open decision D2. (confidence medium)
- [decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas, because approvals, interview questions and question escalation live there. Task escalation (task-escalated) stays in task-execution and reaches the operator through the same inbox. (confidence low)
- [strategize A1] Ideas is classified supporting, not core (decision D1 is open). Its 24 events are the transitions of 1 fixed idea state machine; the judgment work (research, interview, assumptions, spec, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model, not by fleetd code. Scored diff 6, cplx 5. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A2] Core stays the minority: 2 of 6 subdomains (task-execution, integration). Ideas would make 3 of 6, which is half, not a minority (ticket rule for this run). (confidence medium)
- [connect A5] Agent hand-offs (assumptions.md, plan.yaml, result.json, questions, exit.json) are files: atomic, immutable and read in the pass, so they are at-least-once and idempotent on path and content hash (design: Workspace layout and file protocol). (confidence high)
- [organise A2] 1 deployable unit, the horch binary, holds all 6 contexts as modules inside horch-core. The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34; understand C1, N6; decompose N1). Decision D1 records the options. (confidence high)
- [organise A4] The data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose. (confidence medium)

## Verification metrics

- Business (G3): count of tasks that exist outside a committed, validated plan, plus count of processes that planned 2 ideas at once. Target 0.
- Business (G3): count of ideas past awaiting_approval whose approved_sha256 does not match the current assumptions.md (I7). Target 0.
- Structural: count of ledger writes to ideas, plans or questions tables that come from code outside the ideas module (organise N2). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [understand Q8] This repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10), and plan validation refuses a project with no declared fast gate. Which command is the fast gate of this repository?
- [discover Q1] Which feature does an idea with no --to belong to between capture and the first assumptions (H7)?
- [discover Q2] What is the time limit of a worker question before it escalates, and does it pause outside working hours (H10)?
- [discover Q4] Where on the timeline does daemon supervision and adapter conformance belong: in executing, in its own phase, or off the idea timeline (D2)?
- [decompose Q3] Which inbox holds an escalated task for the operator: the ideas context (with approvals and questions) or task-execution? The design puts everything for the operator in 1 place but names no owner.
- [strategize Q1] Is ideas a core subdomain? The idea dispatcher is a fixed state machine in code, but G3 and the value proposition 'rough ideas in, approved plans out' depend on it (decision D1).
- [connect Q5] Does the sub-orchestrator answer a worker question with a file in the idea folder or with horch idea note over the command channel?
- [discover H2 near feature-opened - conflict] 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?
- [discover H3 near sub-orchestrator-started - conflict] 'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3).
- [discover H7 near idea-captured - unclear] The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it?
- [discover H10 near question-escalated - unclear] A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours.
- [connect CC2 - coupling, medium] ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas.
- [connect CC3 - coupling, medium] ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back.
- [connect CC8 - coupling, medium] plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons. The operator inbox owner is also open (decompose Q3).
- [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.
- [define Q5] Domain role of ideas (decision D2).
